sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries and damages sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 18-10-2023.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 18-10-2023 at about 4.40 to 4.50 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding by riding motor bike bearing No. KA.01.HT.9239 near BMW bike show room, 80 feet road,
Koramangala, Bangalore, at that time the driver of the Car bearing No.
KA.01.AD.9851 came from Maharaja Junction side towards Sony word and driven the same at very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor bike of the petitioner and caused the accident.
Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to St. John's hospital, wherein petitioner took treatment as an inpatient and for further treatment he was admitted to Manipal hospital, wherein also the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient, he was diagnosed and also underwent surgery.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as a Client Services Manager at Accenture company and earning Rs.51,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries, petitioner is not able to do his work as earlier and suffering from permanent disability and lost his earning capacity.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending Car are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest.

3. Inspite of service of notice, respondent No.2 owner has not appeared before the court, hence,
placed as Exparte.
After service of summons, Respondent No.1 - insurance company has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by contending that, the complaint was filed after delay of one day.

Further it has denied the issuance of policy to the offending Car bearing No. KA.01.AD.9851 and also contended that, the driver of the offending Car was not having valid driving license at the time of accident.
Further it has also denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner, involvement of the offending car in the alleged accident.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant, arbitrary and disproportionate.
Hence, this respondent prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:

sentences.text: Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Car bearing No. KA.01.AD.9851 by its driver, in RTA took place on 18-10-2023 at about 4.50 a.m., on Near BMW Bike Show- room, 80 feet road, Koramangala, Benglauru ?
2. Whether the petitioner is enti- tled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
3 . What Order or Award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to 21.

Further Dr.Shekar M, Orthopaedics Surgeon of Sanjay Gandhi Institute of trauma and orthopaedics is examined as PW.2 and MRT of Manipal hospital is examined as PW.3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P22 to 27.

sentences.text: In spite of sufficient opportunities the respondents have not lead any evidence.

6. Heard the arguments and perused the materials and evidence that are available on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : In the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final orders  for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:
 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as PW.1.

In support of his case, he has produced certified copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar along with sketch, IMV report, IMV notice and reply, wound certificate, Dama report, discharge summary, outpatient records and head of charge sheet which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 12.
9.

On perusal of Ex.P1 - FIR which is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by the petitioner himself by alleging the rash and negligent driving by the driver of Car bearing No.
KA.01.AD.9851.
The contents of Ex.P.1 & 2 are in consonance with the petition averments.
After the registration of FIR, the IO has conducted spot mahazar and sketch as per Ex.P3 & P4.

On perusal of spot mahazar at Ex.P3 the accident spot is near to the junction wherein the petitioner was proceeding straight and it is found that the driver of the Car bearing No. KA.01.AD.9851 has changed his lane from right side towards left side and caused the accident.

Further Ex.P.5 is the IMV Adithya G V vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116246203/
3 report wherein it is found that the petitioner's motor cycle bearing No. KA.01.HT.9239 has got damages in its front head light doom assembly and left side rear view mirror and in the same way the offending Car bearing No. KA.01.AD.9851 has got damages in its front left side bumper and bonnet.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The contents of Ex.P3, P4 & P5 helped the petitioner to prove the negligence of the driver of Car bearing No. KA.01.AD.9851 in the alleged accident.

10. The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 insurer vehemently argues that there is an inordinate delay of 1 day in lodging the FIR and the same cannot be brushed aside lightly, instead has to be construed as a circumstance showing that the case is an afterthought and the offending vehicle is implicated in the case even though it is not involved in the accident.
But not every delay would move this court to view the case of the petitioner doubtfully.
Because there might be genuine circumstances that could have contributed to the delay.
In fact only if the delay is left unexplained the same needs to be viewed seriously.
11. No doubt in the facts of this case, the accident occurred on 18-10-2023 at about 4.40 to 4.50 a.m.
but the FIR was lodged on 19-10-2023 and hence it is evident that the FIR is lodged after one day of occurrence of the accident.

But the informant in the Ex.P2 first information it is stated that soon after the accident the petitioner was shifted to St John's hospital and thereafter shifted to Manipal hospital and underwent with treatment and also as there was no one to look after the petitioner

,
they were unable to give the complaint immediately.

Further the Ex.P8 is the wound certificate also depicts that on 18-10- 2023 itself the petitioner was taken to Manipal hospital for treatment with history of RTA between two wheeler Vs. four wheeler at about 4.30 a.m. of 18-10-2023.
The contents of wound certificate helped the petitioner to prove the alleged accident and also it shows that the delay of 1 day is backed with genuine reasons.

Hence the delay of one day, in the light of reasons assigned by the PW.1 and also as mentioned in the Ex.P2, complaint, Ex.P8 wound certificate and Ex.P10 discharge summary it cannot be considered as inordinate.

12. Further the petitioner also summoned and examined the MRT of the Manipal hospital as PW.3 wherein he produced the copy of MLC and police intimation which are marked as Ex.P25 & P26 which also evidentiates that on 18-10-2023 at about 2.30 p.m itself the petitioner was taken to Manipal hospital for treatment with history of RTA between two wheeler Vs. four wheeler at about 4.30 a.m. of 18-10-2023.
The police intimation was also issued on the same day.
Thereby the delay is properly explained and no grounds are made out to disbelive the case of the petitioner only on the grounds of one day delay.

13. Ex.P9 is the charge sheet also came to be filed on the driver of the offending Car bearing No.
KA.01.AD.9851 for the offences punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC wherein, the IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of driver of Car bearing No. KA.01.AD.9851.

By producing these documents, the petitioner prima-facie established the occurrence of accident and also the alleged negligence of the driver of the Car bearing No. KA.01.AD.9851.
14.

Wherefore in the absence of any cogent evidence which could rebut the assertions made by PW-1 on oath supported by Ex.P-12 which is the charge sheet and the documents annexed therewith, this court should not have any impediment to conclude that the said documents prima-facie suffice to Adithya G V vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116246203/
4 hold that accident, occurred due to rash and actionable negligence on the part of the driver of Car bearing No. KA.01.AD.9851.

sentences.text:
The view taken by this Court that the police records are prima- facie proof in support of the case of the petitioner, is supported by the decision rendered in Kishan Gopal and another Vs. Lala and others reported in 2013 (4) T.A.C 5 (S.C.), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has categorically held thus:
"In view of the aforesaid facts, the Tribunal should have considered both oral and documentary evidence referred to supra and appreciated the same in the proper perspective and recorded the finding on the contentious issue No. 1 & 2 in the affirmative.

entities.text: Kishan Gopal and another Vs. Lala and others reported in 2013 (4) T.A.C 5 (S.C.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But it has recorded the finding in the negative on the above issues by adverting to certain statements of evidence of AW-1 and referring to certain alleged discrepancies in the FIR without appreciating entire evidence of AW-1 and AW-2 on record properly and also not assigned valid reasons in not accepting their testimony.

The Tribunal should have taken into consideration the pleadings of the parties and legal evidence on record in its entirety and held that the accident took place on 19.07.1992, due to which Tikaram sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same and the case was registered by the Uniara Police Station under Sections 279 and 304-A, IPC read with Sections 133 and 181 of the M.V. Act against the first and second respondents.

The registration of FIR and filing of the charge- sheet against respondent Nos.1 & 2 are not in dispute, therefore, the Tribunal should have no option but to accept the entire evidence on record and recorded the finding on the contentious issue Nos.1 and 2 in favour of the appellants''.
(Emphasis supplied by me)

15. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the inc ident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

entities.text: Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105,
where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the rider of the offending van.

sentences.text: 16. In view of the ratio laid down in the authorities referred to above and applying the settled principle of law to the case at hand, which is further supported by the oral and documentary evidence adduced by PW-1, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident leading to this case indeed occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of Car bearing Adithya G V vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116246203/

. During the course of cross examination of petitioner, except a suggestion nothing has been elicited so as to disprove the case of the petitioner.
There are no material evidence to prove that the petitioner's negligence was the reason for the said accident.
No rebuttal evidence is placed by the respondents.
17. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 18-10-2023 which is caused by the driver of the Car bearing No. KA.01.AD.9851.
There is no reasons to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
18.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the respondent No.2.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
19. The petitioner has produced wound certificate as per Ex.P8 which shows that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Further, the petitioner has also produced discharge summary as per Ex.P10.

On perusal of the same it shows that, petitioner took treatment as an inpatient at Manipal hospital from 18-10-2023 to 21-10-2023 for a period of 4 days and sustained right hip inter trochanteric fracture and also underwent operation for CRIF with PFN AII right femur.
The petitioner examined one doctor Shekar, who assessed the disability.

As per the evidence of PW.2 doctor the petitioner has sustained injury to right hip with pain and swelling who has also produced the disability report which reveals that the petitioner has sustained the permanent physical disability of right lower limb at 45.43% and to the whole body at 15.14%.

20. According to the petitioner he was working as a Client Services Manager at Accenture company and earning Rs.51,000/- p.m. To prove his avocation and income, the petitioner has produced Ex.P13 pay slips, Ex.P15 IT returns and Ex.P17 invoice.
21.

While determining the compensation this court has to look into the pain and sufferings, medical expenses, diet, food, nourishment, attendant and conveyance charges and loss of amenities and enjoyment of life that the PW-1 has suffered, which are discussed herein below:
(A) TOWARDS PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
The petitioner has relied upon Ex.P.8 & P10 - wound certificate and discharge summary, which make it crystal clear that PW-1 has sustained grievous injury.
The petitioner was admitted to Manipal hospital from 18-10-2023 to 21-10-2023 for a period of 4 days.

Hence keeping in mind the injuries mentioned in wound certificate and discharge summary, it can be said that the petitioner must have undergone some Adithya G V vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116246203/
6 amount of physical pain and sufferings, for which, an amount of Rs.70,000/- can be held to be just and proper compensation under this head.
(B) TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES:

entities.text: Adithya G V vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner has produced the medical bills marked at Ex.P19 amounting to Rs.36,860/- and advance bills marked at Ex.P20.
On perusal of Ex.P19, Sl.

No.1 bill,
out of Rs.1,83,197/-, Rs.25,000/- is paid by the petitioner and remaining Rs.1,58,197/- is paid by the Medi Assist India Private Limited and another two bills amounting to Rs.2,774/- and Rs.3,390/- were pharmacy bills which are to be reimbursed.
On perusal of Ex.P20, Sl No.1 to 3 & 7 were paid towards advance deposit and Sl No.4 to 6 were pharmacy bills which were to be reimbursed.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for reimbursement of Rs.33,790/- by rounding off the same the same to Rs.34,000/-.

(C) TOWARDS DIET, FOOD, NOURISHMENT:
As already observed the Ex.P-8 & 10, makes it amply clear that the petitioner underwent treatment for the injuries sustained by him.
During the said period the petitioner might have taken assistance from others and taken diet food.
On consideration of the injuries sustained by the petitioner this Tribunal is of the opinion that it is just and proper to award an amount of Rs.40,000/- under this head.
(D) TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNING CAPACITY ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:
It is necessary to note that the loss of future earning capacity cannot be presumed and has to be proved with cogent evidence.

But interestingly the petitioner though claims that he is unable to do any work and has become permanently disabled he has not put in any efforts to prove the disability by examining the doctor, who treated him.
At the time of cross-examination also the PW.1 admitted that he is still working in Accenture company and he is getting the salary.
The petitioner has produced the Ex.P13 pay Slip which is for the month of August to October 2023 wherein net pay for the month was Rs.46,159/-.
The accident was on 18-10-2023.

As admitted by the PW.1 is still working in the same company and no evidence is placed by the petitioner by showing that due to the permanent disability caused to the petitioner by the accidental injuries is removed from service and unable to continue with the work thereby sustained financial loss.

In the judgment reported in 2020(4) KCCR 2621 between Sri Nandish K. V/s United India Insurance Co. Ltd. & another wherein it is held that no compensation could be awarded towards the loss of earning capacity if physical disability do not effect Adithya G V vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116246203/
7 claimant's capacity to work.

sentences.text: These answers given by the PW.1 evidentiates that the petitioner is continued in the service and no disability is caused which effects his earning capacity.

Hence, this court has no option but to hold that the petitioner has not suffered any permanent physical disability which has resulted in reduction of his salary and hence he is not entitled for any compensation under this head.

(E)
TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
The petitioner has not made out any evidence or grounds to hold that he sustained the loss of income during the laid down period.
At the time of cross- examination the petitioner stated that he was on the earned leave for 30 days but no evidence is placed to show that he applied for the earned leave.
Hence, in the absence of any evidence, petitioner is not entitled for any amount under the head of loss of income during laid up period.
(F) TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES AND ENJOYMENT OF LIFE:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
The petitioner examined one doctor Shekar, who assessed the disability.

As per the evidence of PW.2 doctor the petitioner has sustained injury to right hip with pain and swelling who has also produced the disability report which reveals that the petitioner has sustained the permanent physical disability of right lower limb at 45.43% and to the whole body at 15.14%.
The said amount of permanent disability certainly causes problems in day to day life of the petitioner.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.60,000/- under this head.
g) Towards future medical expenses: PW.2 stated that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants which may cost around Rs.25,000/-.
By looking to the nature of injuries sustained the treatment taken, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.20,000/- under this head.
h) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 4 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the fracture as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e., Rs.4,000/- in total as the petitioner has spent 4 days in the hospital.
) i) Towards Vehicle and general damages:

The petitioner has produced Ex.P17 the invoice dated 19-12-2023 which shows about the repairs done to the petitioner's motor cycle bearing No.
KA.01.HT.9239.
The said Ex.P17 bills is of Rs.36,157/- wherein several damages and allied repairs were done to the petitioner's motor cycle bearing No. KA.01.HT.9239.
Except producing Ex.P17 bill the mechanic or the surveyor are not examined to substantiate that the said repairs are connected to the damages caused to the said motor cycle in the accident.

The accident was caused on 18-10-2023 Adithya G V vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116246203/
8 and the said vehicle was repaired between 16-12-2023 to 19-12-2023.

sentences.text: The said Ex.P17 invoice is belongs to authorized dealers and service of KTM bikes.
As per Ex.P17 bill the said repair amount was paid by cash by the petitioner.
By considering the same the said amount of Rs.36,157/- is need to be reimbursed to the petitioner.

23. To sum up the above discussion, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following:
A) Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 70,000/-

B) Towards Medical expenses Rs.
34,000/- C) Towards diet, food and Rs. 40,000/-
nourishment D) Towards loss of future earning NIL capacity E) Loss of income during laid up NIL period F) Towards loss of amenities and Rs. 60,000/-
nourishment G) Future medical expenses Rs. 20,000/-
h) Attendant charges Rs. 4,000/-
i) Towards Vehicle damages Rs. 36,157/-
 Total Rs. 2,64,157/-
23.
Liability:- According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 is the insurer, respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending Car bearing No. KA.01.AD.9851.
The respondent No.1 in its objection statement has denied the the issuance of policy to the offending car.

Even though the respondent No.1 insurance company has appeared and filed written statement by denying the issuance of policy to the offending Car has neither produced any documents nor lead evidence and the police has also not invoked any sections in the charge sheet by stating that the offending car was not having insurance policy as on the date of accident.
As per Ex.P7 IMV reply the owner of the offending Car bearing No,. KA.01.AD.9851 given reply by furnishing the policy number also.
As per Ex.P7 the said offending car was duly insured with respondent No.1.
No other grounds are made out by showing the violation of policy conditions by respondent No.2 owner.

Hence, the respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.1 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.2 owner.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
24.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total Adithya G V vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116246203/
9  compensation amount of Rs. 2,64,157/-
(Rupees Two lakhs sixty four thousand one hundred and fifty seven only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
